headline: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends public reception in Shillong; lays foundation stones for projects worth over ₹1,000 crore
fullText:
Vice President's Secretariat

Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends public reception in Shillong; lays foundation stones for projects worth over ₹1,000 crore

Every State, village and citizen must become ‘Viksit’ to realise Viksit Bharat by 2047: Vice-President

Vice-President recalls former Lok Sabha colleague late P. A. Sangma as a great leader and Parliamentarian

07 SEP 2026 7:25PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today attended a public reception organised in his honour by the people and Government of Meghalaya at Soso Tham Auditorium, Shillong. He expressed gratitude for the warm welcome and said he would always stand with the people of Meghalaya in the State’s development journey.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced a public reception organised in his honour by the people and Government of Meghalaya at Soso Tham Auditorium, Shillong today.

The Vice President laid the foundation stones for five projects worth over ₹1000 crores. These include… pic.twitter.com/OZqJPC1g2Y

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 7, 2026

The Vice-President highlighted Meghalaya’s rich cultural heritage, natural beauty and unique social institutions, including its matrilineal heritage. He said the State’s vibrant grassroots institutions reflect India’s diversity and democratic traditions. Recalling his former Lok Sabha colleague, late Shri P. A. Sangma, he described him as a great leader and an outstanding speaker who made a significant contribution to parliamentary democracy.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said true secularism means respecting each other’s thoughts an beliefs. He emphasised that people must live together with mutual respect and harmony. He also stressed that development must be inclusive and no section of society should be left behind.

Highlighting the importance of connectivity, the Vice-President said every effort is being made to connect remote villages with towns and cities. He noted that over 46,000 km of rural roads have been constructed in the North-East under PMGSY in the last decade, with expenditure of over ₹47,000 crore. He also appreciated Meghalaya’s reform-linked MoU under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

The Vice President laid the foundation stones for five projects worth ₹1,010.95 crore. These include the New Shillong Water Supply Scheme Phase II, Part A (₹850.58 crore) under the Urban Challenge Fund, two road connectivity projects under NESIDS, a 30-bedded AYUSH facility at Shillong Civil Hospital and a 132/33 KV substation at Mawkhanu under PM-DevINE.

He also inaugurated the Maternity and Children’s Hospital at Nongstoin, completed at a cost of ₹31.05 crore under the National Health Mission. He said the projects, together worth about ₹1,042 crore, will strengthen water supply, connectivity, healthcare and power infrastructure in Meghalaya.

The Vice-President appreciated the State Government’s initiatives in infrastructure and tourism, including the homestay programme, CM-Elevate and Green Meghalaya. He congratulated Chief Minister Shri Conrad K. Sangma, his Council of Ministers and the people of Meghalaya for the State’s progress.

Speaking on the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised that progress must be inclusive, leaving no section of society behind, while preserving Meghalaya’s rich environment, culture and traditions. Referring to the State’s living-root bridges and the landscapes of Sohra and Mawsynram, he said Meghalaya offers valuable lessons in living in harmony with nature.

Chief Minister Shri Conrad K. Sangma, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Prestone Tynsong and Shri Sniawbhalang Dhar, Minister Shri Sanbor Shullai, Chief Secretary Dr. Shakil P. Ahammed and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

headline: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah presents the President’s Colour to Goa Police in Panaji
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah presents the President’s Colour to Goa Police in Panaji

The conferment of the President’s Colour on the Goa Police is a national recognition of its eight decades of dedicated service and valour

Goa Police has efficiently discharged its responsibility of safeguarding the state’s extensive coastline, ensuring the safety and security of tourists and making a significant contribution to strengthening the economy

In coming days, 1930 helpline number will become a strong shield for protecting the country against all forms of cyber fraud

AI-based call agent launched by Goa Police for 1930 helpline will register complaints in all languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution and route them to the appropriate authority

Police response time under Goa Police emergency helpline service 112 has been reduced from 18 minutes to just 8 minutes

New Nayaya Sanhitas incorporate aspects such as technology, sensitivity, prioritisation and the capacity to deliver speedy justice, marking a major upgradation of policing

In just one year, Goa Police increased its conviction rate by 30% , this has increased from 23% to 53%

Home Minister Shri Amit Shah pays homage to the immortal martyrs of the Goa Police

A roadmap has been prepared for 2026–2029 to build a ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat’, under this roadmap, India will be made free from narcotics

The Home Minister expressed confidence that the Goa Police will also emerge as a leading force in combating narcotics

Union Home Minister expresses confidence that Goa Police will also perform well in combating narcotics

07 SEP 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today presented the President’s Colour to the Goa Police in Panaji, the capital of Goa. On the occasion, Goa Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant, Union Minister of State for New and Renewable Energy Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Union Home Secretary, Chief Secretary of Goa, Director General of Police of Goa, and several other dignitaries were present.

Addressing the gathering, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that it was a matter of pride for him to present the President’s Colour to the Goa Police. He said that after eight decades of distinguished service, the Goa Police today stands alongside several other police forces of the country, proudly bearing the honour bestowed by the President of India. Shri Shah said that police forces of the states that have been awarded the President’s Colour have received this prestigious honour for their glorious history, professional excellence, courage, discipline and dedication. He said that Goa is a small yet extremely important state. With the formation of the state, the Goa Police was entrusted with the responsibility of ensuring a safe city, safe community and secure maritime border. He said that since the formation of the state, the Goa Police has successfully discharged all three responsibilities and made a significant contribution to national security.

Shri Amit Shah said that the foremost prerequisite for a developed nation is to ensure complete internal security and the security of its borders. He said that Goa has the distinction of being entrusted with the responsibility of ensuring both internal security as well as border security. He said that the responsibility of safeguarding Goa’s extensive maritime boundary rests on the shoulders of the Goa Police. Discharging this responsibility efficiently, the Goa Police has done commendable work in ensuring the safety and security of tourists and contributing to a strong economy.

On the occasion, the Home Minister paid his respectful tributes to the immortal martyrs who laid down their lives in the line of duty. He specifically paid homage to police personnel Balaram Shinde, Abhishek Sher, Shailesh Gaonkar and Vishwas B. Deykar, and said that their dedication had made a significant contribution to earning this honour for the Goa Police.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that India’s outreach in global diplomacy is expanding steadily with each passing day. He said that over the past year, the global diplomatic landscape has witnessed serious turbulence due to the Russia-Ukraine war, followed by the conflict involving Iran in the Gulf region. In such a challenging environment, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi travelled to 22 countries in a single year, while the heads of state of around 15 countries visited India. Shri Shah said that at a time when the entire world was grappling with economic uncertainty and struggling to sustain its economic growth due to global instability, India maintained its economic momentum through sustained dialogue and strategic partnerships. He said that concrete agreements were reached across a range of sectors, including defence, technology, energy, investment and trade.

Union Home Minister said that by 2026, India had concluded nine Free Trade Agreements (FTAs). These agreements have now been established as effective trade arrangements with 38 countries. The agreements with the United Arab Emirates, Austria, Australia, the United Kingdom, Oman, New Zealand and the European Union have given a fresh impetus to India’s trade. He said that this is reflected in the fact that India’s GDP growth rate reached a remarkable 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of this year. He said that India has not only achieved economic growth but has also contributed to the global community in several ways. These include Vaccine Maitri, sharing the achievements of its Digital Public Infrastructure with the world, and extending assistance to several countries in the areas of disaster relief and capacity building.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India’s diplomacy has today established a distinct position for itself on the global stage. He said that whenever a major global issue arises, the world now looks to the views and perspective of the Prime Minister of India on the matter. Shri Shah said that after a long interval, it is Prime Minister Modi who has restored this stature and recognition to India. He said that Prime Minister Modi has placed before the nation the resolve to build a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He said that the vision of a Viksit Bharat initially faced several challenges and skepticism, but, in a short span of time, it has transformed into the collective resolve of 140 crore Indians. He said that every Indian is now confident that by 15 August 2047, India will emerge as the world’s foremost nation in every field.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that with the expansion of the digital economy, the threat of cyber fraud is being felt across the world, and India is no exception. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has himself initiated direct dialogue with all the states to address this challenge. He said that in the coming days, the 1930 helpline number will serve as a strong shield against all forms of cyber fraud and provide robust security across sectors. He said that the Goa Police has taken a step forward in this regard by introducing an AI-based call agent for the 1930 helpline. In this initiative, the Goa Police is ahead of other states in the country. He said that the helpline will enable complaints to be registered in Konkani, Marathi and Hindi. At the same time, the service will also facilitate the registration of complaints in other Indian languages and route them to the appropriate authorities. Shri Shah said that a large number of tourists from across the country and the world visit Goa. Therefore, demonstrating his vision, the Chief Minister ensured that the AI agent was not restricted to Konkani and Marathi alone, but was expanded to include all the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. He said that this is an important and visionary step for the benefit of tourists as well.

Shri Amit Shah said that the Goa Police has been doing commendable work in every field since its inception. He said that excellence in sports has been a distinctive hallmark of the Goa Police. He said that the International Police Sports Championship will be held in India in 2029, featuring sporting events for police and fire services personnel as well. Union Home Minister called upon all personnel of the Goa Police to ensure that India does not lag behind in the medal tally at this prestigious event. He urged them to begin preparations from now and participate in the championship with full enthusiasm. He said that the Goa Police should prepare to excel not only in football but also in other sporting disciplines. He said that in view of Goa’s long coastline and its population of more than 15 lakh, it is extremely important for the police force to remain physically fit and agile. He said that sports are a powerful means of keeping police personnel physically fit, capable and alert.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that over eight decades, the Goa Police’s commitment and guiding motto of peace, service and justice have continued to make Goa safer. This is why the Goa Police has consistently earned appreciation not only from the people of Goa but across the country. The conviction rate was earlier 23 per cent; now, convictions are being secured in 53 per cent of FIRs, which is a major achievement.

Under this roadmap, the target is to make every village and city across India free from narcotics, with the participation of all concerned departments and all state governments. He expressed hope that the Goa Police will emerge as a leading force in combating narcotics as well.

headline: Union Environment Minister calls for Grassroot-level Public-Participation to tackle Air Pollution in NCR
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Union Environment Minister calls for Grassroot-level Public-Participation to tackle Air Pollution in NCR

First-of-its-kind Dialogue brings together Mayors and Local Body Representatives from 63 NCR cities to take Clean Air Pledge

Scientific, Data-driven approach to Air Pollution Control and Effective Waste Management must reach the Grassroots; Public Representatives to take Lead: Shri Bhupender Yadav

07 SEP 2026 7:08PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for strong grassroot-level public participation to tackle air pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR), while urging Mayors and representatives of urban local bodies to take the lead in driving the clean air mission. The dialogue, involving Mayors and Local representatives from 63 NCR cities, marks the first instance of such a large-scale engagement organised by the Ministry with elected representatives of local bodies on the issue of air pollution.

Shri Yadav emphasised that a scientific and data-based approach to air pollution control must reach the grassroots, with public representatives playing a central role in translating action plans into effective implementation on the ground. He encouraged Mayors and local representatives to lead by example and mobilise citizens to prevent avoidable pollution and ensure cleaner, healthier urban environments. He added that Urban Local Bodies are the first responders and can bring phenomenal change with guided actions, hence have a very important part to play in this issue.

Highlighting the rapid expansion of urban areas and the resulting challenge of solid waste generation, the Minister stressed the need for effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and Construction & Demolition (C&D) Waste Management Rules, 2025 on the ground. He called upon public representatives to familiarise themselves with the powers and responsibilities of local bodies in air pollution control and solid waste management, and to take the first positive steps to create replicable examples for citizens.

Shri Yadav urged local bodies to increase green cover by planting local and drought-resistant grass species along roads to help contain dust pollution. He also called for greater avenues for public participation in ensuring effective cleaning, preventing plastic use and biomass burning, and checking pollution from non-conforming industries and vehicles.

The Minister informed the gathering that more than 25 continuous review meetings have been conducted at the Union level with NCR municipal bodies and State Governments. He also highlighted his engagements with the Chief Ministers of NCR States and the preparation of detailed action plans to tackle air pollution. He urged public representatives to coordinate closely with municipal bodies and ensure effective implementation of these plans at the grassroots.

Shri Yadav highlighted that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, a centralised institutional mechanism, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), has been created for enforcement of air quality management measures in NCR. He assured the local bodies that the Ministry and CAQM would extend full technical support, including access to its technical repository and action plans, to strengthen implementation at the grassroots level.

The meeting ended with the Union Minister administering a Clean Air Pledge to all the present public representatives and taking the lead to work with the citizens in their areas in the direction of effective air quality management. Earlier, two presentations were given to the attendees on 'Air Pollution Control measures in Delhi-NCR', along with one on ‘Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026’ and ‘C&D Waste Management Rules, 2025’. This was done to inform the public representatives about the salient features of the initiatives being taken by the Government, as well as to create awareness amongst them about their duties, responsibilities and powers in the fields of Air Pollution Control and Solid Waste Management.

headline: Ministry of Rural Development Organises National-Level Workshop on “DDU-GKY 1.0 Projects”
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

Ministry of Rural Development Organises National-Level Workshop on “DDU-GKY 1.0 Projects”

States and Union Territories share best practices and deliberate on project-documentation challenges

Technical sessions focus on MIS-related issues and demonstrate the MIS completion Module

07 SEP 2026 6:56PM by PIB Delhi

A two-day National-Level Workshop on the "Completion of Projects under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 1.0" was organised at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), Pusa, New Delhi, by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, on 7–8 September 2026. The workshop brought together senior officials of the Ministry, representatives of States and Union Territories, and technical experts from Central Technical Support Agencies to review the projects of DDU GKY 1.0 to evolve a coordinated approach to declare formal closures after completion of documentation.

DDU-GKY is a flagship placement-linked skill development programme of the Ministry of Rural Development under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). The programme aims to enhance the employability of rural youth through market-oriented skill training and placement, thereby supporting sustainable livelihood opportunities.

The workshop was attended by senior officials of the Ministry of Rural Development, along with representatives of State and Union Territory implementing agencies and technical experts from NABARD Consultancy Services (NABCONS) and the National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR). On the first day, participants deliberated extensively on operational and technical challenges in project completion, best practices, case studies, and the roles and responsibilities of various stakeholders.

The workshop commenced with an inaugural session. Delivering the inaugural note, Shri Pawan Kumar, Director (Rural Skills), called for a project-specific, action-oriented approach to take action on all pending projects, stressing timely bottleneck resolution and adherence to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). In her opening remarks, Ms. Jayasree M.G., Joint Secretary (Rural Skills-II), called for a coordinated, time-bound and campaign-mode approach to completion of documentation of over 2,000 DDU-GKY 1.0 projects, and highlighted priorities under DDU-GKY 2.0, including achieving at least 70% placement and strengthening employment retention.

Following the inaugural session, participants attended a technical session in which NABCONS and NIRDPR made presentations on the completion of documentation of projects under DDU-GKY 1.0, focusing on best practices, case studies, challenges, possible solutions, and the roles and responsibilities of stakeholders involved in the process. The session provided participants an opportunity to identify practical approaches for addressing pending issues and ensuring a systematic completion process.

Representatives from Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Mizoram, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal subsequently shared their experiences and presented the status of project completion in their respective States and Union Territories. The State-wise deliberations provided a platform for peer learning and exchange of effective practices, while also highlighting implementation-level challenges and areas requiring coordinated action among the Ministry, States/UTs and other stakeholders.

The workshop concluded with the consolidation of key learnings and priority areas identified during the deliberations. All participating States and Union Territories reaffirmed their commitment to working in close coordination with the Ministry and technical agencies to ensure completion of documentation and a transparent, accountable and time-bound execution of projects under DDU-GKY 1.0.

THE DAY IS NOT FAR WHEN WOMEN WILL ACCOUNT FOR OVER 50 PERCENT OF PUBLIC SERVICES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

FOCUS MUST SHIFT FROM MERELY PROVIDING SUPPORT TO EMPOWERING WOMEN TO SHAPE POLICIES AND LAWS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

INDIA CANNOT PROGRESS TOWARDS A DEVELOPED NATION WITHOUT THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

07 SEP 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today highlighted the significance of greater representation of women in democratic institutions, referring to the provision of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies as a historic need. Observing the growing presence of women across various public services and professions, Shri Birla said that the coming years would witness a new generation of women leaders emerging across political, administrative, and social spheres. He added that the day is not far when women will account for over 50 percent of public services.

Shri Birla made these observations while inaugurating a two-day All-India Capacity Building Workshop on the theme "Gender-Responsive Governance," organized by the National Commission for Women (NCW) in Faridabad today.

Mentioning that the focus must now shift from merely providing support and opportunities to women towards enabling them to actively shape policies, programmes, and laws, Shri Birla stressed that women should themselves participate in determining the legislation required to address their concerns and aspirations. Referring to the constitutional commitment to equality and various legislative measures undertaken for women’s safety, empowerment, and self-reliance, he highlighted that institutions such as the NCW have an important role in identifying emerging challenges and facilitating solutions. He emphasized that women legislators—through the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, Panchayats, and Municipalities—can play a decisive role in bringing women's concerns before appropriate fora and ensuring that laws respond to ground-level realities.

Shri Birla also stressed that India cannot progress toward the goal of a developed nation without the economic and social empowerment of its women, who constitute nearly half of the country’s population. Every woman, he said, should have opportunities for employment, economic independence, and social empowerment. He called upon women legislators to deliberate on effective policies, schemes, and legislative measures that can strengthen women economically and socially, particularly those facing deprivation and hardship. The experiences and successful initiatives of different legislatures, he suggested, should be shared so that best practices can be replicated nationwide. Furthermore, he underlined the need to enhance awareness among women about the laws and institutional mechanisms available to address their concerns, particularly in vulnerable areas.

Noting that women have always been at the forefront of India’s transformation—from the freedom movement and nation-building to strengthening democratic institutions—Shri Birla emphasized that the programme provides an essential platform for women legislators to exchange experiences, ideas, and perspectives, thereby strengthening their leadership capabilities. The participation of women legislators from various States and Union Territories, he noted, demonstrates the significant role they play in giving voice to women's aspirations through legislative forums, and he urged participants to sharpen their skills to fulfill this mandate.

Emphasizing the importance of dialogue in a vibrant democracy, Shri Birla said that the challenges and aspirations of the people are best addressed through continuous discussion and consultation. He underlined that sensitivity is a core strength of women’s leadership, fostering a deeper understanding of people’s concerns and a greater capacity to find effective solutions. A sensitive and responsive work culture, he added, can contribute significantly to addressing social challenges and strengthening democratic institutions. Advancing women’s leadership, he concluded, must remain a collective resolve, expressing hope that sustained efforts will lead to women increasingly occupying leadership positions across every sphere of national life.

headline: e-FAST India, an initiative of NITI Aayog, launches PACT to support accelerated zero-emission freight deployment in India
fullText:
e-FAST India, an initiative of NITI Aayog, launches PACT to support accelerated zero-emission freight deployment in India

07 SEP 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

New platform will aggregate freight demand across India by continuous engagement with ecosystem stakeholders to facilitate scaled deployment and strengthen the commercial case for zero-emission trucks. The 5th e-FAST India Summit also introduced the ZET Marketplace to unlock business, financing and charging partnerships.

Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog today launched the Platform for Aggregating Clean Transport (PACT) at the 5th e-FAST India Summit 2026, marking a significant step towards accelerating the deployment of zero-emission trucks in India. The platform was launched in the presence of Shri V Umashankar, Secretary, MoRTH; Dr. Hanif Qureshi, AS, MHI; Ms Archana Mittal, PD, Electric Mobility, NITI Aayog; Shri Pawan Mulukutla, ED, WRI, and around 250 participants from across the industry, finance and freight ecosystem.

A flagship initiative under the e-FAST India platform, PACT is designed to aggregate freight demand from shippers, Logistics Service Providers (LSPs) and other ecosystem stakeholders and translate it into deployment opportunities across identified freight corridors. By bringing together shippers, LSPs, vehicle manufacturers, financiers, charge point operators (CPOs) and other ecosystem partners, the platform aims to improve demand visibility, support charging infrastructure planning and strengthen the commercial case for electric medium- and heavy-duty vehicles (e-MHDVs).

The launch comes at a time when India’s electric freight market is gathering pace. E-freight vehicle deployments increased more than fourfold, from 201 vehicles in FY25 to 826 in FY26. Today, over 3,000 e-MHD trucks are in operation across the country. Sustaining and scaling this momentum will require coordinated action to aggregate demand, expand charging infrastructure, improve access to finance, and provide greater certainty for fleet operators and investors.

Speaking at the Summit, Chief Guest Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog, said, “While significant progress has been made in building domestic EV manufacturing capacity and supportive policy mechanisms, the next phase of growth will depend on our ability to address ecosystem-wide challenges through collaboration. The launch of PACT and the ZET Marketplace brings together various ecosystem stakeholders on a common platform. As freight electrification gains momentum, innovative financing models, corridor-based charging infrastructure, and market-driven partnerships will be critical to accelerating the commercial adoption of e-trucks and strengthening India's clean mobility future.”

Shri V. Umashankar, Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) said, “Accelerating electric freight mobility will require innovations in logistics operations, financing charging infrastructure, and battery governance. Measures such as battery health monitoring systems and new operating models for high-utilization vehicles can improve transparency, strengthen resale value, reduce financing risks, and unlock greater investment. With growing industry interest and rising demand, India is well positioned to build a scalable and commercially viable electric trucking ecosystem that advances both logistics competitiveness and energy security.”

The Summit also introduced the ZET Marketplace, an interactive business-engagement platform connecting e-truck manufacturers, LSPs, CPOs, financiers, and technology companies. The Marketplace enabled participants to showcase products, explore commercial opportunities and develop partnerships needed to move zero-emission freight projects from intent to implementation.

The plenary and technical sessions at the Summit deliberated on financing and de-risking mechanisms, charging infrastructure, policy priorities, and lessons from early deployments. Together, the discussions underscored the need to move beyond individual pilots towards coordinated, commercially viable deployment at scale.

With each evolving year, the e-FAST India platform is moving from building market readiness towards enabling deployment. Through initiatives such as PACT and the ZET Marketplace, NITI Aayog and its partners aim to convert freight demand, investment interest and technology readiness into scalable zero-emission freight projects across India.

Key Announcements

• Launch of the Platform for Aggregating Clean Transport (PACT)

• ZET Marketplace

About NITI Aayog

NITI Aayog is the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India, tasked with catalyzing economic development and fostering cooperative federalism by involving State Governments in the economic policy-making process.

About e-FAST India

e-FAST India (Electric Freight Accelerator for Sustainable Transport - India) is a NITI Aayog-led platform that brings together government and industry stakeholders - including OEMs, logistics service providers, financiers, shippers and charge point operators - to accelerate the transition to zero-emission freight in India, particularly in the medium- and heavy-duty vehicle segments.

headline: From Substance Dependency to a New Beginning: Garry's Journey towards Recovery, Self-Reliance and Social Reintegration
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Substance Dependency to a New Beginning: Garry's Journey towards Recovery, Self-Reliance and Social Reintegration

07 SEP 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

Substance dependency can disrupt education, relationships and future opportunities, while emotional stress, social stigma and limited access to support can make recovery more difficult. Timely counselling, treatment and rehabilitation can provide individuals with the guidance and confidence needed to rebuild their lives.

Demonstrating the impact of support under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), Garry (name changed), a 27-year-old resident of Tseminyu district in Nagaland, is maintaining sobriety, engaged in self-employment and gradually reintegrating into society. His journey reflects the role of sustained rehabilitation, family involvement and community support in enabling positive transformation.

Belonging to the Scheduled Tribe community and educated up to middle school, Garry faced several challenges due to substance abuse. Emotional stress, lack of direction and negative peer influence gradually led to substance dependency, adversely affecting his personal life, education, social relationships and future opportunities.

His educational progress was interrupted, while his confidence and motivation were significantly affected. Substance dependency also limited his ability to lead a stable and productive life. His family experienced emotional and financial strain while managing daily needs and rehabilitation-related support.

Social stigma and limited awareness within the community created additional barriers during Garry's recovery. Geographical and accessibility challenges further delayed access to counselling, treatment and rehabilitation services during the initial stage.

Despite these difficulties, Garry aspired to rebuild his life, become self-reliant, regain the trust of his family and community, and contribute positively to society. He desired a second chance to lead a healthy and meaningful life free from substance dependency.

With support from family members, community leaders and the District De-Addiction Centre (DDAC), Tseminyu, Garry gradually accepted rehabilitation and recovery support. The intervention under NAPDDR provided him with a safe and supportive environment, emotional guidance and the motivation needed to overcome substance dependency and rebuild his life.

Through DDAC Tseminyu, Garry received individual counselling, psychological support, de-addiction and rehabilitation services, motivational and behavioural guidance, family counselling and community support interventions. Awareness programmes and psychosocial care formed an important part of the assistance provided to him.

During the rehabilitation process, Garry was encouraged to adopt healthy habits, restore his self-confidence and reconnect positively with his family and community. Continuous follow-up monitoring helped support sustained recovery and social reintegration.

The intervention contributed to improvements in Garry's mental well-being, discipline and social behaviour. His relationship with his family and community improved, and he began participating in productive and responsible activities within the community.

At present, Garry is maintaining sobriety, actively participating in productive activities and continuing his journey towards social reintegration with renewed hope and responsibility. He is self-employed and now serves as an example of positive transformation through rehabilitation and support under the NAPDDR scheme.

Garry's journey demonstrates how counselling, treatment, psychosocial care, family involvement and community encouragement can help an individual move beyond substance dependency. With sustained support, he has progressed towards a healthier, meaningful and self-reliant life.

headline: Jute: India’s Golden Fibre
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Jute: India’s Golden Fibre

Sustaining livelihoods through innovative policy interventions

07 SEP 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

India leads global raw jute production, supporting millions of livelihoods while advancing sustainable industrial growth. India produced 76 lakh bales of raw jute and 12.80 lakh MT of jute goods in FY 2025-26. During the same year, India exported 22,700 MT of raw jute worth ₹225.11 crore and 1,71,300 MT of jute goods worth ₹3,155.27 crore. Government interventions have strengthened farmer incomes, modernised the value chain, and promoted product diversification. Jute's biodegradable nature and expanding applications make it a key alternative to synthetic materials. Innovation, market expansion, and digital technologies are positioning India's Golden Fibre as a globally competitive and environmentally responsible industry.

India’s Golden Fibre Industry

Jute is one of the most significant natural fibres in India, valued for its wide range of applications and environmental sustainability. In the trade and industrial context, jute and mesta are collectively classified as raw jute due to their comparable end uses. Mesta is a bast fibre crop cultivated as a cost-effective alternative to jute, particularly in drier agro-climatic regions. Owing to its characteristic golden colour and silky lustre, jute is commonly referred to as the “Golden Fibre”.

India is the world’s largest producer of raw jute. The Third Advance Estimate of Production of Food Grains (2025-26) highlights the growth of jute and mesta production from 88.02 lakh bales in 2024-25 to 94.03 lakh bales in 2025-26. India is also the leading jute goods-producing country globally, accounting for about 75% of estimated world production, as of July 2026. The jute industry has a heavy industrial base in India’s eastern region, especially West Bengal. This industry provides direct employment to approximately 3.70 lakh workers in organized mills and diversified jute units. It also sustains the livelihoods of nearly 40 lakh farm families engaged in jute cultivation. As of December 2025, India has 120 composite jute mills, and West Bengal alone houses 89 of them, the highest among all states.

India continues to be fully Atmanirbhar in the production of jute goods, with domestic output adequately meeting national demand. In FY 2025-26, the domestic consumption of jute goods was 12.05 lakh MT. This accounts for 94% of the total production of jute goods, which was 12.80 lakh MT. Further, India exported 1.71 lakh MT of jute goods valued at ₹3,155.27 crore in FY 2025-26. In terms of raw jute, India exported 22,700 MT worth ₹225.11 crore in FY 2025-26.

Tracing the History of Jute Production in India

The history of jute in India can be traced back to the third century BC. However, it emerged as a significant commercial commodity during the British Colonial period owing to its strategic military applications. The East India Company established numerous jute mills in Bengal, positioning the region as a centre for jute cultivation and processing.

India’s independence in 1947 and the subsequent partition significantly disrupted the integrated jute economy of Bengal. Nearly 80 percent of the jute-growing areas became part of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh). But most jute mills remained in India, resulting in an acute shortage of raw material for processing in these mills. To address this imbalance, the government launched the "Grow More Jute" campaign in September 1949. The farmers were encouraged to shift from paddy cultivation to jute. Consequently, India’s raw jute production more than doubled from 6.7 lakh tonnes (1951-52) to 14.56 lakh tonnes (1961-62). The Jute Packaging Act, 1987, further strengthened the sector by mandating the use of jute sacks for packaging essential commodities. This move ensured a stable market for Indian jute farmers. Over time, jute emerged as a strategic green fibre, contributing to rural livelihoods and environmentally sustainable industrial development.

Presently, West Bengal contributes the largest share of raw jute cultivation in the country, followed by Bihar, Assam, Odisha, and Jharkhand. Jute is generally sown during March-April and harvested within 100–110 days. It thrives under hot and humid conditions with rainfall between 700–1,500 mm during the crop-growing period. Given these agro-climatic requirements, its cultivation is concentrated mainly in eastern and northeastern India and is predominantly rainfed. The crop is primarily grown by small and marginal farmers.

Why is Jute an Important Natural Fibre?

Jute is a biodegradable and recyclable natural fibre characterised by its rapid growth, cost-effectiveness, and wide availability. It is strong, durable, breathable, and highly versatile, with applications spanning packaging, construction, agriculture, and industrial textiles. Jute also possesses favourable functional attributes, including thermal and acoustic insulation, high moisture absorption, and low static generation. It blends well with both natural and synthetic fibres, facilitating a wide range of value-added and textile applications.

Can Jute be Eaten as Food?

Jute leaves have long been consumed as a vegetable in regions such as Africa, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia. In Japan, jute leaves are widely recognized and consumed as a health food. Nutritionally, jute leaves are rich in vitamins, carotenoids, calcium, potassium, and dietary fiber, underscoring their value as a functional food source. Proven technologies have also been developed for anti-oxidant herbal drink and health care products from jute leaf.

Jute Geotextile: The Fabric of Sustainable Infrastructure

Jute Geotextile (JGT) is a versatile, diversified jute product belonging to a class of technical textiles. It can be applied in many fields like civil engineering, soil erosion control, road pavement construction and protection of river banks. JGT can be made from jute fibers through special treatment and weaving processes.

It is increasingly gaining acceptance due to its functional effectiveness, environmental compatibility, favourable techno-physical properties, and price competitiveness. From an ecological standpoint, JGT is fully biodegradable, thereby improving soil structure and fertility. Moreover, JGT is globally recognized as an effective natural solution for soil stabilization, erosion control, and ecological restoration in degraded landscapes. This is because it helps in regulating the micro-environment by maintaining lower soil temperatures and reducing surface disturbance. Hence, it supports seed germination and early plant establishment.

Applications of Jute Geotextile

Jute Geotextile has gained recognition as an effective natural material for diverse applications in civil engineering, soil conservation, and infrastructure development:

It is widely utilized for slope protection in earthen embankments, hill cuttings, riverbanks, canals, and rainwater harvesting structures. This is because of its high initial tensile strength, and surface roughness enhances soil stabilization and mitigates erosion.

In road and haul road construction, as well as in railway track formation, JGT improves load distribution and control settlement. This reduces maintenance requirements and lifecycle costs.

Its use in concealed drainage systems, particularly in hilly regions, enables regulated water flow while preventing soil migration. JGT is also used to stabilize soft soils through prefabricated vertical drains, accelerating consolidation and enhancing bearing capacity.

In recent years, the National Jute Board has been actively engaged in developing and promoting jute geotextiles as an engineering material. The Board provides technical support to end users, including guidance on design specifications, procurement processes, testing protocols, and installation practices.

Indian Contingent Showcases Jute Apparel at Commonwealth Games 2026

Jute-viscose-blended apparel was worn by the Indian athletes and team members at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. The clothing has been developed by the National Jute Board. The apparel was designed by the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), New Delhi. This initiative highlights the potential of 100 percent biodegradable jute-viscose blended fabric as a sustainable and innovative textile solution. This initiative has provided global visibility to India's jute industry while highlighting the craftsmanship of Indian manufacturers.

From Farm to Market: Government Interventions for the Jute Industry

The government has undertaken a series of policy measures reflecting a sustained commitment to strengthening India’s jute sector. These include upward revisions of the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for raw jute. The MSP of raw jute has been fixed at ₹5,925 per quintal for FY 2026-27. This would ensure a 61.8 percent return over the all-India weighted average cost of production. This marks an increase of around 147% from the MSP of raw jute in FY 2014-15 (₹2,400per quintal). The MSP amount paid to jute farmers has also increased over time. For the period of FY 2004-05 to FY 2013-14, the amount paid was ₹441 crores. It has increased to ₹1,342 crores from FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26.

The government has also implemented the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities) Act. It specifies the commodities and the extent to which they are mandatorily required to be packed in jute packaging material. The government mandated jute packaging for 100% food grains and 20% sugar in jute bags.

Jute Corporation of India

The Jute Corporation of India Ltd. (JCI) is the sole nodal agency for implementing the MSP policy for raw jute. It safeguards jute farmers’ interests by procuring directly from farmers when market prices fall below the MSP. JCI’s Departmental Purchase Centers (DPCs), which are situated in rural areas, purchases raw jute directly from the farmers. JCI has around 110 DPC’s in states of West Bengal, Assam, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tripura.

The government has integrated its efforts for supporting jute cultivation and processing under the National Jute Development Programme.

National Jute Development Programme (NJDP)

The National Jute Development Programme (NJDP) is the umbrella scheme for the development and promotion of the jute sector. It is being implemented by the National Jute Board with an outlay of ₹485.58 crore from FY 2021–22 to FY 2025–26. It focuses on enhancing farm productivity and farmer incomes, as well as diversification through two key components: JUTE-ICARE and the Jute Diversification Scheme. The programme also supports seminars, exhibitions, and awareness campaigns to promote jute as an alternative to plastics.

National Jute Board (NJB)

The National Jute Board (NJB)serves as the nodal agency for the development, promotion, and diversification of the jute sector across the value chain. Its key functions include:

improving cultivation and fibre quality,

enhancing productivity and standardisation,

promoting domestic and export markets,

supporting research and value-added product diversification, and

strengthening MSMEs and artisans through capacity building and market development.

JUTE-ICARE (Improved Cultivation and Advanced Retting Exercise) Scheme

The JUTE-ICARE scheme, launched in FY 2015–16, aims to enhance jute productivity and fibre quality. This is being achieved through scientific cultivation, mechanisation, and improved retting techniques. It supports small and marginal farmers through subsidised certified seeds, field demonstrations, and mechanized interventions. It is being implemented in collaboration with the Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibers (CRIJAF) and the Jute Corporation of India. The scheme also facilitates the construction of retting ponds through convergence with the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana and Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana.

Jute Diversification Scheme

The Jute Diversification scheme includes schemes supporting jute processing, marketing, sales.

Intervention for Supporting Jute Processing: Jute Raw Material Bank (JRMB)

The Jute Raw Material Bank facilitates the availability of raw jute materials for the unorganized sector and small production units for manufacturing of jute diversified products. This is done by supplying raw jute materials at the economic rate of mill-gate price plus actual transportation costs. The scheme supports artisans, women SHGs, and MSMEs engaged in jute-diversified products by providing regular access to quality raw materials. This further promotes rural livelihoods.

Interventions for Manufacturing, Marketing, and Sales

The Jute Diversification Scheme promotes value addition, modernisation, and market expansion through multiple sub-schemes:

Capital Subsidy for Acquisition of Plant & Machinery: Offers a 30% subsidy on machinery costs for jute mills and MSMEs producing JDPs.

Jute Resource-cum-Production Centres: Cluster-based training and production centres for artisans, women SHGs, entrepreneurs, NGOs, members of cooperative societies etc.

Jute Retail Outlets: Support retail and showroom sales of JDPs with 25% sales assistance (up to ₹9 lakh per unit).

Production Linked Incentive for JDP Exports: Provides exporters with incentives linked to raw material usage in jute diversified products exported and its value realisation on exports.

Interventions for Branding, Quality Assurance, and Market Promotion

Jute Mark India Logo

The Jute Mark India logo symbolises authenticity, quality assurance, and sustainability in jute and jute-blended products. The stylised sheaves of jute within a structured framework represent natural fibre strength, craftsmanship, and standardisation across the value chain. The Jute Mark India logo certifies compliance with quality standards and verifies jute content in blended products. This enhances consumer confidence and strengthens brand recognition.

Domestic Marketing Initiatives

The government organised over 57 regional jute fairs across major cities in FY 2025-26, such as the India International Trade Fair, Surajkund Mela, and Bharat Tex.

Jute Handloom Enterprise: From SHG to Export Markets

Branding, exhibition-based promotion, and structured market access have boosted field-level outcomes for jute enterprises. Such are the stories of Bharatiya Gramothan Sanstha, Rishikesh (Uttarakhand), Hayden Hall Institute, Darjeeling (West Bengal), Jute Artisans Guild Association, Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) and Rural Organisation for Social Action, Cuttack (Odisha). Trained under the National Jute Board programmes, they leveraged mentoring and market linkages to enter organised jute handloom production. They started participating in major trade fairs such as IITF New Delhi, Tex-Trends India, New Delhi and GiftTex Show, Mumbai. This enabled direct buyer interactions for them, secured bulk export orders, and strengthened their marketing skills. As a result, their members individually started earning more, with notable improvements production capacity and social recognition.

Digital and Technological Interventions Across the Supply Chain

Since 2016, the entire operations of procurement and supply of jute sacking (food grain) bags is

being managed by the Office of Jute Commissioner. To facilitate these operations, an end-to-end e-governance software portal, viz. JUTE-SMART has been developed and implemented by the Office of Jute Commissioner in November 2016. Till August 2026, 303 lakh bales of B.Twill Jute Bags (@500 pieces of bags/bale) worth more than ₹1.00,000 crores (approx.) have been procured by more than 20 State Procurement Agencies incl uding Punjab, Haryana, Odisha, Telangana, West Bengal, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and FCI etc., through this portal.

In 2026, JUTE-SMART has been further upgraded for digitizing various processes in the supply chain. Various stakeholders have been onboarded, like transporters, raw jute traders, and importers. Registration of raw jute traders, importers and jute mills has been completely digitized. The required returns are also completely online for improving the ease of compliance.

Jute Crop Information System

The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO), through the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), has developed the Jute Crop Information System. It has been developed in collaboration with Jute Corporation of India and National Jute Board. The system functions to monitor jute cultivation using remote sensing and field data. As part of this initiative, two key tools have been developed:

BHUVAN JUMP: a mobile app for on-field jute monitoring, and

PATSAN (Prospective Assessment of Jute Using Mobile App-Based Field Observations): a web-based platform that provides near-real-time jute surveillance and analytics to support informed decision-making by officials and stakeholders.

Market Development & Promotion Scheme

The government, under the National Jute Development Programme, has been implementing the Market Development & Promotion Scheme. This scheme supports the Jute Diversified Product (JDP) entrepreneurs/exporters in promotion and sale of JDPs in the domestic/export market.

Workers’ Welfare Scheme (Scholarship Scheme)

National Jute Board Act, 2008 provides to “secure better working conditions and provisions and improvement of amenities and incentives for workers engaged in the jute industry”. In line with the same, NJB provides scholarship/incentive support to the girl children of the workers of Jute Mills/JDP-MSME units on passing out Secondary and Higher Secondary examinations.

A Sustainable Future with Jute

India's jute sector has evolved into a key driver of sustainable and inclusive development. It supports millions of farmers, workers, artisans, and entrepreneurs across the value chain. Policy support, innovation, and improved production have strengthened the sector's competitiveness. Jute contributes to rural livelihoods, environmental sustainability, and industrial growth. Its growing relevance reflects India's transition towards greener and sustainable materials. Continued investment, innovation, and community participation will unlock the sector's full potential.

Schedule for bye-elections to 05 (Five) Assembly Constituencies of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and West Bengal and 01(One) Parliamentary Constituency of Assam

07 SEP 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission has decided to hold bye-elections to fill vacancies in the following Assembly Constituencies:

Sl. No. | Name of State | Number and Name of AC/PC | Reason of vacancy

1. | 35-Madurantakam (SC) | Resignation of Tmt. Maragatham

Tamil Nadu | AC | Kumaravel

West Bengal | Kabir

6. | Assam | 09-Nagaon PC | Resignation Bordoloi | of Sh. Pradyut

The Schedule for the bye- election is enclosed at Annexure-I.

1. ELECTORAL ROLLS

Commission firmly believes that pure and updated electoral rolls are the foundation of free, fair and credible elections. Hence, intensive and sustained focus is placed upon improving its quality, health and fidelity. After the amendment in Section

14 of the Representation of the People Act-1950 by the Election Laws (Amendment) Act-2021, there is a provision of four qualifying dates to enroll as a voter in a year. Accordingly, the Commission conducted the Special Summary Revision/ Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Roll in the States.

Name of States/UT | Number and Name of AC/PC | Date of Final Publication of E-Roll of the AC/PC

Tamil Nadu | 35-Madurantakam (SC) AC | 23.02.2026

101-Dharapuram (SC) AC | 23.02.2026

Puducherry | 09-Thattanchavady AC | 14.02.2026

West Bengal | 70-Rejinagar AC | 28.02.2026

210-Nandigram AC | 28.02.2026

Assam | 9-Nagaon PC | 10.02.2026

However, the process of continuous updation of electoral rolls will continue till the last date of filing nominations, with respect to proximate qualifying date, in respect to applications received till 10 days before last date of filing nomination.

2. ELECTRONIC VOTING MACHINES (EVMs) & VVPATs

The Commission has decided to use EVMs and VVPATs in the bye-election in all the polling stations. Adequate numbers of EVMs and VVPATs have been made available and all steps have been taken to ensure that the poll is conducted smoothly with the help of these machines.

3. IDENTIFICATION OF VOTERS

Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) shall be the main document of identification of a voter. However, any of the below mentioned identification documents can also be shown at the polling station:

MGNREGA Job Card;

Passbooks with photograph issued by Bank/Post Office;

Health Insurance Smart Card issued under the scheme of Ministry of Labour/Ayushman Bharat Health Card;

Driving License;

Smart Card issued by RGI under NPR;

Indian Passport;

Pension document with photograph;

Service Identity Cards with photograph issued to employees by Central/State Govt./PSUs/Public Limited Companies;

Official identity cards issued to MPs/MLAs/MLCs; and

Unique Disability ID (UDID) Card, M/o Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India.

4. MODEL CODE OF CONDUCT

The Model Code of Conduct shall come into force with immediate effect in the district(s) in which the whole or any part of the Assembly constituency going for election is included, subject to provision of the instruction vide Commission’s

letter No. 437/6/1NST/ECI/FUNCT/MCC/ 2024/ (BYE ELECTIONS) dated 2nd January, 2024 (available on the Commission's website).

5. INFORMATION REGARDING CRIMINAL ANTECEDENTS

Candidates with criminal antecedents are required to publish information in this regard in newspapers and through Television channels on three occasions during the campaign period. A political party that sets up candidates with criminal antecedents is also required to publish information about criminal background of its candidates, both on its website and also in newspapers and Television channels on three occasions.

Commission vide its letter No. 3/4/2019/SDR/Vol. IV dated 16th September, 2020 has directed that the period specified will be decided with three blocks in the following manner, so that electors have sufficient time to know about the background of such candidates:

Within first 4 days of withdrawal.

Between next 5th - 8th days.

From 9th day till the last day of campaign (the second day prior to date of poll)

(Illustration: If the last date for withdrawal is 10th of the month and poll is on 24th of the Month, the first publication of declaration shall be done between 11th and 14th of the Month and second and third publication shall be between 15th and 18th and 19th and 22nd of that Month, respectively.)

This requirement is in pursuance of the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Writ Petition (C) No. 784 of 2015 and Writ Petition (Civil) No. 536 of 2011.

The political parties shall also publish in newspapers and its official social media platforms and upload in its website, the details and the reasons for selecting candidates having criminal background within 48 hours of selection of such candidate. The details are contained in letter no. 3/4/2021/SDR/Vol.III dated 11.01.2022 available on the

Commission’s website.

headline: Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog launches PACT and ZET marketplace, urges stategic electrification of India’s freight sector
fullText:
Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog launches PACT and ZET marketplace, urges stategic electrification of India’s freight sector

07 SEP 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Rajiv Gauba delivered the inaugural address at the 5th E-Fast India Summit 2026. During the event, he marked a significant milestone in India's clean mobility journey with the launch of the Platform for Aggregating Clean Transport (PACT) and the Zero Emission Truck (ZET) Marketplace.

In his address, Shri Gauba noted that e-FAST has evolved over four years from a forum for dialogue into a vehicle of coordinated action, mirroring the shift in India's clean mobility discourse from intent to implementation. Shri Gauba emphasised that transitioning to electric mobility is an economic, environmental, and strategic imperative essential for achieving the global commitment of Net Zero by 2070 and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047. He highlighted that accelerating electric vehicle adoption is vital for the nation's energy security and improving citizens’ quality of living.

He outlined the progress achieved through government initiatives including the PLI schemes for Automobiles and Advanced chemistry cells, expansion of public charging infrastructure owing to investments made by the Oil Marketing Companies, and demand-side schemes such as FAME, PM e-DRIVE, PARIVARTAN and PM e-Bus Sewa, supporting a rise in EV sales.

Addressing the heavy-duty commercial sector, Shri Gauba noted that while heavy trucks represent only 3-4% of the vehicle fleet, they contribute to over a third of transport-sector carbon emissions. He identified structural fragmentation among logistics operators, high financing costs, and the absence of coordinated corridor planning as the key constraints holding back the market, noting that PACT and the ZET Marketplace have been designed to close precisely this gap through demand aggregation, financing innovation and corridor-based projectization.

He observed that only around 800 heavy-duty electric trucks were sold in 2025, underscoring the need for strategic electrification of key freight corridors given that 70% of India's freight moves by road. He called for blended finance mechanisms, leasing models, and stronger data systems to bring the cost of capital for electric trucks closer to diesel equivalents.

Shri Gauba called upon logistics providers, manufacturers, charge point operators and financiers to engage with the platform in shaping the corridors, financing instruments and commercial models that will define electric freight in India.

He observed that the summit reflects a wider institutional lesson that extends well beyond freight, that in complex, capital-intensive sectors, government is at its most effective not when it seeks to allocate outcomes directly, but when it builds systems that allow markets to discover them, describing PACT as one such enabling mechanism.

headline: From Financial Hardship to Doctoral Achievement: Manika Mandal's Journey through Higher Education
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Financial Hardship to Doctoral Achievement: Manika Mandal's Journey through Higher Education

07 SEP 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

Financial constraints can make the pursuit of higher education and academic research particularly difficult. For scholars from economically disadvantaged families, fellowship assistance can provide the stability and resources required to continue research and realise long-term academic aspirations.

Demonstrating the impact of support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Smt. Manika Mandal, a 33-year-old scholar from South 24 Parganas district in West Bengal, successfully completed her Ph.D. despite financial hardship and limited educational resources. Her journey reflects the role of fellowship support in enabling scholars to overcome economic and social barriers in higher education.

Before receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme, Manika faced serious financial difficulties that affected her higher studies and educational research. Her family experienced financial instability and struggled to meet education-related expenses, making it challenging for her to continue advanced studies and sustain her research activities.

Economic hardship and limited access to academic resources created additional educational and social barriers. The expenses associated with doctoral research placed further pressure on the family, while inadequate resources made it difficult for Manika to pursue her academic goals with certainty and continuity.

Despite these challenges, Manika remained committed to completing her Ph.D. Her aspiration was not limited to earning a doctoral degree; she also wished to contribute to society through education and use her academic journey as a means of creating a positive impact.

In April 2017, Manika began receiving fellowship assistance under the NFSC Scheme. She availed fellowship support amounting to approximately Rs. 20 lakh. The assistance supported her Ph.D. studies and research work while helping address the financial difficulties and shortage of educational resources that had previously affected her progress.

The fellowship eased the burden of research-related and education-related expenditure on her family. It provided the financial stability needed to continue her doctoral work and enabled her to remain focused on her long-term academic objectives.

With sustained support under the NFSC Scheme, Manika was able to overcome the barriers that had constrained her higher education and successfully complete her Ph.D. The achievement marked the fulfilment of a major personal and academic goal that had once appeared difficult because of her family's financial circumstances.

At present, Manika is a Ph.D. graduate and her academic accomplishment demonstrates how timely fellowship assistance can help scholars from financially constrained backgrounds pursue advanced education, complete research and move closer to contributing to society through learning and knowledge.

Manika's journey highlights the role of the NFSC Scheme in expanding access to higher education and supporting the academic advancement of Scheduled Caste scholars. Her success stands as an example of determination strengthened by institutional support and educational opportunity.
